key_insight: A GPU-accelerated Eulerian-Lagrangian framework can efficiently simulate both fluid motion and passive or inertial particle transport in 2D incompressible turbulence.
engineering_relevance: This approach is useful for studying turbulent dispersion, preferential concentration, and particle-laden flows where accurate coupling between flow fields and particle trajectories matters.
method: Extend a Fourier pseudospectral Navier–Stokes solver with particle modules
Advance fluid with second-order Adams–Bashforth and particles with fourth-order Runge–Kutta
Couple Eulerian and Lagrangian fields via bilinear, bicubic Catmull-Rom, or bicubic B-spline interpolation
evidence_signal: The framework was verified against analytical solutions and benchmark problems, and transport results showed bilinear interpolation performed nearly as well as higher-order schemes with good particle-number convergence.
watch_item: Because the model is one-way coupled and designed for two-dimensional incompressible flows, it may not capture strong particle-to-fluid feedback or fully 3D effects.
paper_title: A coupled Eulerian Lagrangian approach for fluid and particle dynamics
